title: GitHub Release notes are read from the working-tree CHANGELOG, not the tagged commit (twin of lore-cli LCLI-639)
description:
Quest's twin of lore-cli LCLI-639 (read by ref at opum-ai/lore-cli 1d1ebb89, .quest/tasks/LCLI-639.json). It was found by lore-cli's LCLI-622 reviewer and routed here by opum-agent on 2026-09-28. The pairing is a design point both repos share, not a regression. LCLI-622 recorded it as a MATCH with QCLI-398, because both read the working tree.

Measured on quest-cli dev 30148e9. scripts/github-release.mjs releaseNotesFor() reads join(root, "CHANGELOG.md") from the checkout that promote-release.mjs runs in. This happens at scripts/promote-release.mjs:813, for both the pre-move refusal and the cut. So an uncommitted edit, or an edit landed on dev after the tag, becomes the body of a NEW vX release. Nothing checks the notes against the tagged commit. An EXISTING release is safe, because QCLI-401 refuses differing notes and never edits them. promote-release.mjs already resolves the commit v<X> peels to at :691 (resolveTagCommit), before the notes are read.

Second, theoretical edge, also named in LCLI-639: changelogSection() ends a section at the first later line that starts with "## ", including one inside a fenced code block. A fenced "## " line would silently truncate the release body. Quest's extractor also does not CRLF-normalise the CHANGELOG before splitting, where lore's does. Record that as a known asymmetry to settle in the pairing, not as a separate defect.

This is a paired change. Agree the rule with lore-cli before changing the reader, and cross-read by ref at both final heads, as QCLI-401/LCLI-622 did.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The rule is agreed with lore-cli (LCLI-639): both sides read release notes from the commit v<X> peels to, not the working tree, for both the pre-move refusal and the cut. Mechanism agreed with lore-cli 2026-09-29: each side reads through its own native mechanism from the GitHub API at the peeled SHA, not `git show`, because the promote scripts hold no local-git invocation and a local tag object is not guaranteed at promote time
A test proves a working-tree CHANGELOG edit that is not in the tagged commit does not reach the release body, and the test fails against the pre-change module
A "## " line inside a fenced code block no longer ends a section, or the fence edge is explicitly ruled out of scope with lore-cli, and the two extractors agree either way
lore-cli confirms by ref at both final heads that the notes-source rule and the section extractor give matching verdicts
bun run check exits 0, and a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

plan: 1. Amend AC0's parenthetical from the git-show mechanism to the agreed gh-API-at-peeled-SHA one, and record on this record that the agreement is with lore-cli (LCLI-639).

2. scripts/github-release.mjs: CRLF-normalise the changelog before splitting and make changelogSection fence-aware, with CommonMark for an unclosed fence (runs to EOF). Add a changelog-at-commit source that reads CHANGELOG.md at the peeled SHA through gh api contents with Accept: application/vnd.github.raw, with an injectable fetch seam so tests never touch the network.

3. releaseNotesFor(version, {commit}) reads only from that commit, no working-tree read on any path; promote-release.mjs passes the peeled.commit it already resolves at :763, for both the pre-move refusal and the cut.

4. The standalone repair tool github-release.mjs main() resolves the peel through resolveTagCommit before reading notes, so it cuts the same bytes the next preflight compares; the missing-section refusal names the honest remedies (re-tag, or hand-cut) instead of implying that editing and re-running works, since the tag it reads is immutable.

5. Tests: a working-tree edit absent from the tagged commit does not reach the release body (AC1), and the test fails against the pre-change module; fence vectors (i) unindented, (ii) 2-space-indented, (iii) closed-fence-then-heading still ends, (iv) unclosed fence runs to EOF; CRLF normalisation. Update the source-order needle in test/qcli398-github-release.test.ts, which names the old call shape.
6. Reviewer pass, bun run check exits 0, then land via a branch and PR into dev and send lore-cli this head plus the extracted bodies for the AC3 cross-read.
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED on fix/QCLI-407-notes-from-tagged-commit (off origin/dev 7f4aa511), commit b3c462e. The notes now come from the commit v<version> peels to, read through the GitHub API, on every path: the pre-move refusal, the cut, and the standalone repair tool.

WHAT CHANGED. scripts/github-release.mjs gains changelogAt(commit), which reads repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/contents/CHANGELOG.md?ref=<sha> with Accept: application/vnd.github.raw and --hostname github.com, returning {text, commit, error} and never throwing -- the same shape check-breaking-bump.mjs already reads a peer's changelog with. releaseNotesFor(version, {commit}) returns {ok: true, notes, title} or {ok: false, detail}; its working-tree option (changelogPath) is gone entirely, so there is no longer a way to ask for the old behaviour. changelogSection normalises CRLF before splitting and is fence-aware, with an unclosed fence running to EOF; the heading search is deliberately left fence-unaware, because the rule agreed with lore-cli governs where a section ENDS. promote-release.mjs passes the peeled.commit it already resolved at the bundle gate -- one read, reused by the cut -- and the missing-section refusal now names re-tagging or a hand cut, because the tag it reads is immutable and editing-then-re-running cannot reach it. github-release.mjs main() resolves the peel itself through resolveTagCommit, so the repair tool cuts the same bytes the next preflight compares against. The qcli398 source-order test's needle was updated: that call's shape changed, not its position, and the order it asserts is unchanged.

PAIRING, agreed with lore-cli 2026-09-29 before either side wrote code. Rule: the notes body and title come from CHANGELOG.md's bytes at the peeled commit, with no working-tree read on the promote path. Mechanism: each side reads through its own native mechanism from the GitHub API at the peeled SHA -- not `git show`, whose addition would put the first local-git invocation into a flow that has none, and add a tag-not-fetched refusal mode. Identical predicates on both sides: open /^ {0,3}(```|~~~)/, close while open /^ {0,3}(```|~~~)[ \t]*$/, a `## ` line while open does not end the section, an unclosed fence runs to EOF (CommonMark), and a `## ` after a CLOSED fence still ends it. Four vectors are asserted on both sides: (i) unindented fence, (ii) two-space-indented fence, (iii) closed fence then heading, (iv) unclosed fence to EOF.

EVIDENCE. test/qcli407-notes-from-tagged-commit.test.ts, 9 tests: 9 pass / 0 fail post-fix. CONTROL against the pre-change module (origin/dev blob 46b48e7f74a2ca11b0ad7ae490f22f90d2b66513, extracted with git show into a scratch tree together with the pre-change promote-release.mjs -- the two source-layout tests read that file, and without it the whole run died at module scope before any test could fail, which is the same trap as a control that imports a symbol the change adds): 8 fail / 1 pass. The one that stays GREEN is vector (iii), the heading after a CLOSED fence still ends the section -- the property the fix must PRESERVE, not change. So the change reddens exactly the cases it should and leaves the unaffected property alone. bun run check exits 0 at b3c462e: 975 pass / 0 fail across 110 files, up from 966/109, which is exactly this file's 9 tests.

STATUS. AC1 and AC2 are met by the tests above; the reviewer pass AC4 asks for is dispatched and AC3 waits on lore-cli's cross-read at this head.

EVIDENCE, second pass: the real path, and the cross-read.

END-TO-END against a live annotated tag, which the unit tests fake because they inject execFile. `node scripts/github-release.mjs --version 0.11.0` (dry run) answers "release v0.11.0 exists; would mark it latest". The chain resolves the v0.11.0 tag object (84cc917d) to commit eb1d9f466db49f03c763f94c06347e78b969eab5, and that is where the bytes were read. Checked independently rather than taken from the tool's own success line: extracting `## 0.11.0` from CHANGELOG.md at that commit with a separate gh read gives 7906 characters against the stored release body's 7907, differing in exactly one trailing newline, and the existing normaliseNotes comparison trims both -- so the equality holds and the "exists" verdict is genuine rather than a short-circuit. That also shows the migrated path and the old working-tree path produced the same notes for a release cut before this change.

CROSS-READ with lore-cli, provisional at their head c6c248b1 against my b3c462e: they ran the six agreed vectors in-process through their committed extractor, and no row differs once their Keep-a-Changelog heading convention (`## [x.y.z]`, the pre-agreed LCLI-622 difference) is applied. Their extractor is fence-unaware on the heading START too, matching mine, so the agreed rule governs the END only. They confirmed the EOF link-reference trim is a REAL difference and asked me to measure it rather than assume: input "## 9.9.9

notes

[9.9.9]: https://example.com/9.9.9
" gives me body "notes

[9.9.9]: https://example.com/9.9.9" where they trim it -- so the one deliberate asymmetry is measured, and it is inert on quest's file, whose CHANGELOG has no trailing link-reference block. Both heads may still move under a reviewer pass, so AC3 is NOT yet satisfied: it reads "at both final heads", and both will be re-read by ref at the end.

CONTROL PINNING, adopted from lore-cli's correction of their own practice: the pre-change module is pinned by BLOB SHA 46b48e7f74a2ca11b0ad7ae490f22f90d2b66513 (addressable with `git cat-file blob <sha>` and reachable from dev's history permanently) rather than by a ref, because a control reading origin/dev stops being a control the moment the fix merges there. Re-running it needs the pre-change promote-release.mjs beside it as well, or the two source-layout tests kill the run at module scope before any test can fail.

REVIEW OUTCOME, 2026-09-29. One independent reviewer pass (opum-workflow:reviewer) over commit b3c462e, asked to attack four things: that no path still reads a working tree or a mutable ref, that the paired fence rule is implemented as agreed, that the new failure shape does not leak, and that the control is sound. It cleared all four and found six things, all addressed in the commits that follow it.

F2/F3 -- the consequential technical finding, and it was mine: the first cut carried the agreed predicate literally, and that predicate had two holes that this change made WORSE rather than better. A `~~~` line inside a ``` block closed it, so a `## ` inside the block still truncated (the failure the rule exists to remove, incomplete rather than regressed). A fence of four or more markers matched neither predicate and could never close, so the body ran past the next heading -- bounded before, unbounded after. And a fenced `## <version>` that hijacked the section START ran to EOF once the end rule became fence-aware -- also bounded before, unbounded after. Taken to lore-cli with the measurements rather than fixed unilaterally, because the predicate is the paired rule; they reproduced all three and returned a refined rule, now implemented identically on both sides: fence state over the whole document first, open on /^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})/ with the backtick info-string restriction and both character and run length remembered, close only on the same character at AT LEAST the opener's length with nothing but whitespace after, and a fenced heading may neither start nor end a section -- so a changelog whose only `## <version>` line is fenced now refuses instead of cutting the wrong bytes. The deliberate limit (fence state only; no indented-code blocks, no lazy continuation, no container scoping) is recorded in the code as a decision.

F1 -- a consequence of the rule change, filed rather than folded in: re-sourcing the notes moved the QCLI-401 existing-release comparison target with them, so four live releases (0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0, 0.8.0) that were cut or backfilled from a working tree differing from their tag now report a difference instead of being confirmed. Nothing automated reaches them and the forward path matches. The refusal text now names the object it compares -- the section at the tagged commit -- rather than "the CHANGELOG section", because the old wording implied a repair that would destroy later-authored text (0.6.1's and 0.8.0's bodies carry "tagged, never published" where their tag's sections do not). The decision is QCLI-410.

F4 (remedy order: hand cut before re-tag, since a re-tag moves a tag published pages read live), F5 (the release runbook was the operator-facing half of this change and now states the tagged-commit rule, the remedy order and the four affected releases), F6 (a test comment whose stated failure mechanism was true in one control layout and not the other), and two nits (the changelogAt docblock claimed a shape check-breaking-bump.mjs does not have; github-release.mjs spread a result object with a stray `ok` key across a boundary) are all fixed.

EVIDENCE AT THIS STATE. The test file grows to 16 and passes 16/0. Against the pinned pre-change module (blob 46b48e7f) it is now 12 fail / 3 pass, and the three that stay GREEN are exactly the preserved properties -- vector (iii) heading-after-closed-fence, vector (b) longer-fence-bounded-by-next-heading, and the backtick info-string case. So the change reddens what it changes and leaves the rest alone, which is the localisation a reviewer's mutation check is for. bun run check exits 0: 981 pass / 0 fail across 110 files (up from 966/109 before this task). lore check exits 0 (63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings). The reviewer independently reproduced bun run check exit 0 on b3c462e before the fixes.

NOT YET SATISFIED: AC3, which reads "lore-cli confirms by ref at both final heads". Their confirmation so far covers the six original vectors at their head c6c248b1 against b3c462e, which is no longer my head; both sides have moved since, and the re-read at the final heads is the one that counts.

AC STATE AT THE RENEWAL BOUNDARY, 2026-09-29.

MERGED. PR opum-ai/quest-cli#403 squash-merged to dev as f862e962, after all three required contexts (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check) completed success on the exact head 38941580c9de1fad01b188c02f96b59c043373e0 with zero pending required rows on it. Promotion to main follows in PR opum-ai/quest-cli#404.

CHECKED: positions 1, 2, 3 and 5 -- the rule agreed with lore-cli; the test proving a working-tree CHANGELOG edit cannot reach the release body, which fails against the pinned pre-change module; the fence rule; and bun run check exit 0 with the reviewer pass.

OPEN: position 4 -- "lore-cli confirms by ref at both final heads that the notes-source rule and the section extractor give matching verdicts". HALF SATISFIED, and I am not checking it on half. lore-cli confirmed MY final head by ref: they fetched scripts/github-release.mjs at 3894158, plus the qualification helpers it imports, and ran all thirteen vectors through MY committed bytes with their own runner -- my bytes, their runner -- and every row matched the bodies I had reported. That is a cross-read rather than two sessions agreeing. Their own head is NOT final: they wrote that their fence fix was still uncommitted in their checkout, and that their c6c248b1 is superseded precisely because it carries the same three fence defects mine did. So the criterion's "both final heads" clause cannot be satisfied yet, and checking it would assert a verification that has not happened.

WHAT CLOSES IT. lore-cli sends their committed head; whoever is on this repository runs vectors (a)-(g) plus the two extras against it and against this repository's merged dev commit, and confirms both columns match. They asked that the re-stated confirmation be against the LANDED dev commit rather than a branch head, since both are then immutable -- so the object is f862e962, or dev's tip at that later time, not 3894158.

EVIDENCE, all measured here: test/qcli407-notes-from-tagged-commit.test.ts is 16 tests, 16 pass. Against the pinned pre-change module (blob 46b48e7f74a2ca11b0ad7ae490f22f90d2b66513) it is 12 fail / 3 pass, and the three green are exactly the preserved properties -- vector (iii) heading-after-closed-fence, vector (b) longer-fence-bounded-by-next-heading, and the backtick info-string case -- so the change reddens what it changes and nothing else. bun run check exits 0 at 982 pass / 0 fail across 110 files, measured on the merge head. lore check exits 0 (63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings). End to end against the live annotated tag v0.11.0: its tag object 84cc917d peels to commit eb1d9f46, the tool read there, and an independent extraction at that commit equals the stored release body under the existing normaliseNotes comparison (7906 characters against 7907, one trailing newline).

SESSION-BOUNDARY HANDOFF, 2026-09-29 (orchestrator-requested renewal, written AT the boundary). The task is deliberately left In Progress on one criterion; this session did not check it.

STATE. QCLI-407 is LANDED on dev at f862e962 (PR opum-ai/quest-cli#403, squash), and dev is being promoted to main in PR opum-ai/quest-cli#404 -- read main's ref rather than any SHA in this note, because the promotion moves it after this was written. The code and the runbook are delivered. The task stays open on AC position 4 ONLY.

NEXT ACTION, in order. (1) Read lore-cli's head BY REF when they send it -- their fence fix was being committed as this session ended, and their reviewer pass follows it; their c6c248b1 is superseded and must not be used. (2) Run the thirteen vectors against BOTH their committed head and this repository's landed dev commit, not against a branch head: lore-cli asked for the landed object specifically, because both are immutable once on dev. The vectors are (a) tilde inside a backtick fence, (b) a four-marker fence, (c) a fenced heading hijacking the start, (d) three markers inside four, (e) five closing three, (f) the original six A-F, (g) the link-reference EOF case, plus the two extras added here: the only-fenced-heading case returning null, and "```a`b" opening nothing. (3) If both columns match, check AC position 4 and complete the task; if they do not, that is a divergence to settle with lore-cli before either side's rule is called agreed. (4) Land the closure the way QCLI-405's was landed: a small chore branch, a PR into dev, a BARE `gh pr merge <n> --squash` alone in its call, then fetch and read origin/dev.

ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so a successor does not re-derive it. lore-cli confirmed MY final head by ref: they fetched scripts/github-release.mjs at 3894158, plus the qualification helpers it imports, and ran all thirteen vectors through MY committed bytes with their own runner -- every body matched what I had reported, which makes it a cross-read rather than two sessions agreeing. The three fence defects the reviewer found were regressions this change INTRODUCED (a `~~~` line inside a ``` block closed it; a fence of four or more markers could never close; a fenced heading could hijack the section start and then run to EOF), and the refined rule that fixes them is implemented identically on both sides -- whole-document fence state, same character at at-least the opener's length with a whitespace-only tail, the backtick info-string restriction, and a fenced heading neither starting nor ending a section. The one deliberate asymmetry stands as measured: the EOF link-reference trim. lore trims it, quest folds it, and it is inert on quest's CHANGELOG, which has no trailing link-reference block.

QUEUE. QCLI-399 is In Progress and deliberately held for the next pair release, its AC1-AC3 procedure in its earlier notes. QCLI-406 waits on the lore release carrying LCLI-633, then e2e TASK-130. QCLI-410 is new and is the review's consequential finding: four backfilled releases (0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0, 0.8.0) whose stored GitHub Release bodies no longer match their tag's CHANGELOG section, where which body to keep is a judgement because two of them carry later-authored text. Note that TWO tasks are In Progress (QCLI-399 and this one), so the session-end flush will skip its own note -- that ambiguity is real, not a formatting problem, and this note is the handoff instead.

SKILLS for the successor: opum-quest:quest for tracker work, opum-workflow:opum-sdlc for the branch/PR/merge/promote path, opum-workflow:opum-handoff for a further boundary, opum-lore:lore for the runbook (lore sync then lore check; check exits 0 is the definition of done for a docs change). OPAG-722 routing unchanged: operator-bound questions go to opum-agent as an A/B packet, and merges run bare.
